title: Put these in order of how long they take

prereqs.why: This is the ladder itself, and having it in your head is what makes a back-of-the-envelope estimate possible.
The first half of the ladder is the memory hierarchy; the second half is storage and network.

statement:
Six operations, each a thing a server does constantly. Put them in order from **fastest to slowest**.

Approximate figures are fine — the orders of magnitude are what matter, and the gaps between these are large. Nobody should be guessing within a factor of two here; the useful knowledge is which of two things is a hundred times the other.
hints: Start by splitting them into three groups: things that happen inside the CPU and its memory, things that touch a storage device, and things that go over a network.
Within the storage group, one of them has a mechanical arm that has to physically move. That is the slow one, by a lot.
Within the network group, one is limited by the speed of light over thousands of kilometres. Nothing you do in software improves it.

items: A round trip between two machines in the same datacentre
A packet round trip from California to the Netherlands and back
A seek on a spinning disk
A random read from an SSD
